answer: Each epoch every key signs a plume listing how it voted on every ballot. Knoll auditors compare plumes and link any keys whose ballots agree on more than 90% of votes into one cluster. To keep voting, the k-th key in a cluster must lock 100·k² mesa. A lone stranger locks 100 mesa. A bloc of 100 clones voting together locks 33,835,000 mesa, and splitting them to slip past the knoll means scattering the very votes they were created to cast.
